chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad from Abu Ayyub al-Madani from Sulayman al-Ja'fari from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the killing of the hoopoe, the turtledove, the sparrow, and the bee.
ai.seo_question: What animals did the Prophet Muhammad forbid from being killed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes a specific legal precedent (fiqh) for the protection of four distinct creatures: the hoopoe, turtledove, sparrow, and bee. It reflects the Prophetic tradition of preserving biodiversity and highlights the spiritual significance of these animals in Islamic ecological ethics, extending the concept of *haram* (forbidden) to include non-human life forms under divine command.
